title: Splitting 96 Well Plates for gDNA Extraction and Freezing Down
author: Celeste M M. Karch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x79frr6
materials: Tap to lift cells from plate.

steps.title: Wash Cells
steps.instruction: Wash the 96 well plates with 200 µL PBS and aspirate.

steps.title: Detach Cells
steps.instruction: Detach cells using Trypsin and verify detachment.

substeps.instruction: Check under microscope to ensure cells have detached from the plate.

steps.title: Prepare gDNA Extraction Samples
steps.instruction: Collect a portion of the cells for gDNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Add 45 µL mTesR1 to the plate and tap to mix.
Transfer 15 µL to a 96 well PCR plate, maintaining the location of each sample.

steps.title: Prepare Cells for Freezing
steps.instruction: Add freezing media to the remaining cells in the plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 2X Freezing Media (20% DMSO in FBS) to the cell plate and tap to mix.

steps.title: Seal and Label Plate
steps.instruction: Secure the plate to prevent contamination and evaporation.

substeps.instruction: Label the plate on the outside of the tape.

steps.title: Freeze and Store Plate
steps.instruction: Slowly freeze the plate and store at ultra-low temperature.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate in a Styrofoam box.
Fill any open areas with diapers, paper towels, or Kimwipes.
Cover the box and ensure the lid is closed completely.
Store in -80 °C for up to 4 months.
